claims.text: For \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) with \(t>r+s-n\), \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is the unique bigrassmannian \(v_1\cdots v_n\in S_n\) with \(\Des(v)=\{(r\leftrightarrow r+1)\}\), \(\Des(v^{-1})=\{(s\leftrightarrow s+1)\}\), \(v_t=s+1\), and \[ v_{r,s,t,n}=(1,\ldots,t-1,\ s+1,\ldots,s+r-t+1,\ t,\ldots,s,\ s+r-t+2,\ldots,n). \] [source-2@L973-L992|claim=formal-document]
The source sets \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and states that \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is \(r\)-grassmannian and corresponds to the \(j\times i\) rectangle \(i^j\). [source-2@L1354-L1362|claim=formal-document]

In the integral symmetric-function setting, \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\); \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the ideal spanned by \(s_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). The source states that \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of this quotient by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1310-L1325|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

1311: notation and to make more convenient use of symmetric function
1312: identities, we will work within a quotient of the {\it ring of

1314: $$

1316: $$
1317: see \cite[Chapter 1]{Macdonald-symm-fns}, \cite[Chapter 7]{Stanley-EC2}.
1318: The $\ZZ$-basis for $\Lambda$ given by the Schur functions $s_\lambda$ 
1319: has the property that the $\ZZ$-submodule $I_{r,n-r}$ spanned by all $s_\lambda$
1320: with  $\lambda \not\subseteq (n-r)^r$ forms an ideal, and the
1321: map sending $s_\lambda$ to $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ induces an isomorphism
1322: $$
1323: \Lambda/I_{r,n-r} \quad \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \quad \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J}/\ZZ[\xx]^W_+ \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J}

claims.text: Theorem 5.4 sets \[ a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j), \] and gives the two generating sets \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}, \qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\} \] for \(J_v\) as an ideal of \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [source-2@L1380-L1402|claim=formal-document]
Both displayed Theorem 5.4 families have \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements; their degree generating function is \(q^{ij}\qbin{a+b}{a}\). [source-2@L1407-L1421|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1407: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets \eqref{generating-set-one} and \eqref{generating-set-two} for $J_v$,
1408: the shapes $\mu$ indexing the generators $s_\mu$ run through an interval between
1409: the $j \times i$ rectangular shape $i^j$ and the disjoint union of $i^j$ with a 
1410: smaller rectangle of shape $a \times b$ or $b \times a$. 
1411: In \eqref{generating-set-one} the smaller rectangle is to the right
1412: of the rectangle $i^j$, with both top-justified, while in \eqref{generating-set-two} the 
1413: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle $i^j$, with both left-justified.  
1414: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size $\binom{a+b}{a}$
1415: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
1416: have generating function 
1417: $$
1418: \sum_\mu q^{|\mu|} = q^{ij} \qbin{a+b}{a},
1419: $$
1420: where $\qbin{a+b}{a}$ is a $q$-{\it binomial coefficient} or {\it Gaussian polynomial} 
1421: \cite[I.2 Exer. 3]{Macdonald}.

claims.text: The formal conjecture is: “The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem [5.4] are both minimal.” The authors report computer verification only for all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]

With \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Lambda_n\) the graded ring of symmetric functions over \(\mathbb Z\) and \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), the source conjectures that \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators and suspects \[ M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}. \] It states that a proof had eluded the authors. [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]

1517: The size of any minimal generating set of a homogeneous ideal is
1518: well-defined. This is implied by the following well-known fact:
1519: 
1520: \begin{proposition} 
1521: \label{prop:commalgfact}
1522: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and $\Lambda=\oplus_{n \geq 0}
1523: \Lambda_n$ a graded, connected $R$-algebra, meaning that $\Lambda_0
1524: =R$ and $\Lambda_i \Lambda_j \subset \Lambda_{i+j}$.  Let $M$ be a
1525: graded $\Lambda$-module, with degrees bounded below, meaning that
1526: $M=\oplus_{n \geq N} M_n$ for some $N \in \ZZ$, and $\Lambda_i M_j
1527: \subset M_{i+j}$.
1528: 
1529: Then a set of homogeneous elements $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ generate $M$ as a $\Lambda$-module
1530: if and only if their images $\{\bar{m_i}\}_{i=1}^t$ span $M/\Lambda_+ M$ as a $R$-module.
1531: In particular, $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ form a minimal $\Lambda$-generating set with respect to
1532: inclusion for $M$ if and only if $\{\bar{m_i}\}_{i=1}^t$ form a minimal $R$-spanning
1533: set for $M/\Lambda_+ M$.  
1534: \end{proposition}
1535: 
1536: In our setting, the well-definedness follows by setting
1537: $\Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n}$ to be the graded ring of
1538: symmetric functions with ${\mathbb Z}$ coefficients and setting
1539: $M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$, so that the ${\mathbb Z}$-module $M/\Lambda_{+}M$
1540: is a finitely generated abelian group.
1541: %
1542: %Thus in view of (\ref{eqn:badlowerbnd}), for $w\in S_n$, the worst case for the
1543: %number of generators needed in $I_w$ has an {\it exponential}  
1544: %lower bound that accompanies the exponential upper bound of $2^n$ 
1545: %from Theorem~\ref{general-bound}. 
1546: %
1547: % It is plausible to try to apply Proposition~\ref{prop:commalgfact} to prove 
1548: % Conjecture~\ref{minimality-conjecture}, by instead showing that for $M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$,
1549: Thus we conjecture that this abelian group $M/ \Lambda_+ M$ requires
1550: $\binom{a+b}{a}$ generators, and in fact, we suspect that
1551: $M/\Lambda_{+}M\cong {\mathbb Z}^{\binom{a+b}{a}}$.  So far a proof
1552: has eluded us.
